To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the calibration of the DSSSDs can be done by using the data obtained in the horizontal and vertical strips of the DSSD.

a) the use of a double-sided detector allows to improve the detector calibration, b) the use of two different detectors, placed at different angles with respect to the beam direction, allows for particle identification based on the energy loss in the first detector and the energy deposited in the second one, and c) the use of the second detector allows to map the non-uniformities in the thickness of the first one.

1) the DSSSD can be used as two independent detectors and 2) particle identification is improved if the ΔE and E signals from the DSSSD are combined with those of the thick detector, in a way that the energy deposited by the charged particles in the thin detector is used as a reference for the particle energy loss in the thick detector, and the energy deposited in the thick detector is used as an energy reference.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the improvement of the data analysis of standard telescopes, without the need for additional detectors, and with the possibility of using the same telescope for different reactions, with different targets and energies, and for different purposes.
the development of new data acquisition and analysis techniques for the detection systems used for the study of nuclear reactions with radioactive ion beams.
the improvement of the analysis of data from large-area silicon ΔE-E detector telescopes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed improvements are useful and can be applied in the analysis of data from similar experiments.
the proposed methods can be applied for a quick and reliable calibration of large area telescopes, as well as for particle identification.
the proposed methods can be successfully applied for the analysis of the data obtained by the large area telescopes, which are used for the study of nuclear reactions with exotic beams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a proper calibration of the telescope is a prerequisite for the reliable particle identification.
we have developed a method for a more efficient calibration of the detectors and a more precise identification of the reaction products.
the proposed procedures are simple, robust and can be applied to a wide class of experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DSSSDs can be calibrated with a much higher accuracy than previously thought.
a careful analysis of data obtained with large area DSSSD telescopes can improve the quality of results and reduce the amount of time needed for data analysis.
the use of large area silicon detectors, with a large number of readout channels, allows for a more efficient and accurate data analysis.
